## 🚨 SQL Injection Analysis

The provided "username" is a **classic SQL injection payload**:

```sql
admin'; ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS users_pkey CASCADE; DROP TABLE users CASCADE; --
```

**Breaking it down:**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `admin'` | Closes the string literal to break out of the query |
| `;` | Terminates the original `SELECT` statement |
| `ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT ...` | Drops the primary key constraint |
| `DROP TABLE users CASCADE;` | **Destroys the entire users table and all dependent objects** |
| `--` | Comments out the rest of the original query to avoid syntax errors |

## ✅ The SAFE Way to Do This

To look up a user with an unusual username, **always use parameterized queries**:

```python

    "SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE username = %s",
    ("admin'; ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT...",)  # Treated as plain text
)
```

**Node.js (pg):**

client.query(
    "SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE username = $1",
    ["admin'; ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT..."]  // Safe parameter
);
```

WHERE username = $$admin'; ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS users_pkey CASCADE; DROP TABLE users CASCADE; --$$;
```
